title: Lightweight reconciliation & replay lane for affected tenants — quick customer note
content:
TL;DR
We experienced a regional inference jitter window on 2026-03-16 (15:42–16:25 UTC) that caused a subset of tenant requests to receive truncated or partially repeated structured outputs. Impact was limited in scope (estimated 0.3% of total requests in the affected region) but could affect downstream systems that rely on exact structured payloads. This note outlines a lightweight, self-serve reconciliation and replay lane we are rolling out to affected tenants so customers can: 1) verify which requests were affected, 2) re-run deterministic replays where available, and 3) attach operator-provided evidence for audit and compliance.

Why we are sending this note
- Keep customers operational and minimize manual support friction.
- Provide transparent evidence and reproducible replays for tenants that need deterministic outputs for auditing or state reconciliation.
- Offer pragmatic choices (opt-in replay, safe-skip, or manual reconciliation) so teams can pick what's best for their downstream systems.

What happened (short)
- On 2026-03-16 at ~15:42 UTC a routing backpressure event interacted with a transient KV cache eviction that produced a small window where streaming responses were occasionally cut short and retried fragments were concatenated into the final payload.
- Root cause: a subtle interaction between the autoscaler’s eviction policy and streaming session timeout logic; when the KV cache was rehydrated mid-stream, some agents attempted an immediate resume which produced partial duplicates in the output chunk sequence.
- Scope: ~0.3% of requests in region eu-west-1 over ~43 minutes. Few tenants saw full failures; most saw degraded outputs rather than hard errors.

What we are offering to tenants (replay + reconciliation lane)
We have built a lightweight workflow that lets tenants reconcile affected requests without a long support queue. Features:
- Evidence bundle: for each affected request we can provide a timestamped operator trace, session hash, and the raw token chunk stream captured by the runtime. These bundles are cryptographically signed for auditability.
- Snapshot tokens: optional tenant-visible snapshot_token included in request logs. Snapshot tokens map to the captured bundle and can be used for replays.
- Deterministic replay endpoint: a read-only endpoint that accepts snapshot_token and tenant-api-key and returns a deterministic re-execution of the original request against the pinned model and config used at the time of the request. The replay is idempotent and rate-limited to prevent abuse.
- Safe preview: replays can be requested in preview mode where we return both the original affected payload and the deterministic replay side-by-side to help validation.

Customer choices (recommended patterns)
- Option A — Quick verification (recommended for most): Pull evidence bundles for a small sample of requests (10–50) that matter to you, run preview replays, and validate structural parity. If parity is confirmed, mark as safe-skip and continue.
- Option B — Full deterministic replay (recommended if you need exact outputs): For transactions that must be exact (billing, compliance), request a deterministic replay using snapshot_token; consume the result and reconcile in your downstream store.
- Option C — Manual reconciliation: If replays are not suitable (non-deterministic prompts, external side-effectful prompts), we can attach signed evidence you can use for manual adjudication or customer dispute processes.

How to use the lane (step-by-step)
1) Identify affected requests: query the tenant log inspector with filters: time window 2026-03-16 15:40–16:30 UTC, region: eu-west-1, response-flag: stream-truncated.
2) Request evidence bundle: POST /admin/tenant/{tenant_id}/evidence-request with a list of request_ids. You will receive a list of snapshot_tokens (or a note if a request is not replayable).
3) Preview deterministic replay: GET /replay/preview?snapshot_token={token} with your tenant API key in header. Preview returns {original, replay} pair.
4) Accept and ingest: If replay matches, POST /replay/accept to receive a canonical output payload suitable for down-stream ingest (signed and timestamped).
5) If you choose to escalate, open a customer-support ticket and attach the snapshot_tokens; CS will fast-track analysis with engineering.

Limits and safeguards
- Replay retention: evidence bundles and snapshot_tokens will be retained for 90 days from the incident date.
- Rate limits: deterministic replay endpoint is rate limited to 1 replay per second per tenant by default; we can temporarily increase limits for critical reconciliation on request.
- Non-replayable cases: some requests are not replayable (depends on prompt side-effects, external tool calls, or model version pinning). Evidence bundles will indicate replayability.
- Privacy note: replays run against pinned model and the same routing tier; no additional data is used. Replays are audit-logged and accessible only to tenant API-key owners and authorized CS personnel.

Suggested operator wording for status page update (two short variants you can use directly)
Variant 1 (concise): "Resolved — small percentage of requests in eu-west-1 experienced truncated or duplicated structured output during a 43-minute window on 2026-03-16. We have fixed the root cause and are offering a self-serve replay and evidence lane for affected tenants to verify or recover canonical outputs. See our customer note for steps."

Variant 2 (developer-focused): "Resolved — intermittent streaming responses were truncated/concatenated for ~0.3% of requests in eu-west-1 between 15:42–16:25 UTC on 2026-03-16. Root cause fixed; we provide signed evidence bundles and a deterministic replay endpoint so teams can validate or recover affected responses. Contact support to increase replay limits."

Samples and FAQ (quick)
Q: Will a replay always return the same output?
A: If the request is marked replayable and the model+config were pinned at the time of the original call, the deterministic replay will reproduce the original output. If any external tool hooks or time-dependent outputs were present, the replay may differ and will be marked non-deterministic.

Q: I see a snapshot_token but preview shows mismatch. What now?
A: Use the evidence bundle and preview mismatch to run a manual reconciliation or escalate to CS; include the snapshot_token and example diff. We’ll attach operator traces and kernel-level chunk logs to aid triage.

Q: Is there a risk replays could expose data from other tenants?
A: No. Replays are tenant-scoped and gated by the tenant API key; evidence bundles are signed and tenant scoped. No cross-tenant data is accessible.

Operational notes for CS and SRE (internal quick checklist)
- Validate the list: engineering will provide a CSV of affected request_ids and tenant_ids by end of day 2026-03-18.
- Enable preview: CS can toggle preview mode for a tenant for up to 48 hours for accelerated reconciliation; open internal ticket to request toggle.
- Escalation path: if a tenant reports discrepancies after replay, route to ENG-APPLIED-ML (owner: Samir Patel) with snapshot_token and evidence bundle id.

Next steps (what we will do)
- Engineering: finalize the signed-evidence format and extend retention to 180 days for enterprise tenants that request it (ETA 2026-04-01).
- Product: add a small UX flow in the Console for evidence bundle requests and replay previews (ETA Q2 2026).
- CS: notify tenants that are high-risk (billing, legal) with one-off outreach and offer increased replay rate limits and retention.

Contact and escalation
- Primary CS contact: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai).
- SRE on-call (for replay infra): Priya Nair.
- Engineering owner (replay infra): Samir Patel.

Appendix: example customer-facing snippet you can paste into an email
"Hello — on 2026-03-16 we saw a small number of streaming responses in eu-west-1 that were truncated or contained duplicated fragments. We have fixed the underlying issue and created a lightweight reconciliation lane so you can request cryptographically-signed evidence bundles and deterministic replays for affected requests. If you rely on exact structured payloads for downstream processing or compliance, let us know the request_ids and we will provide snapshot_tokens and fast-track support."

Notes to self (work-in-progress)
- Decide replay retention policy for enterprise tenants (90 days vs 180 days) and update SLA addendum.
- Add telemetry flag to distinguish cache-eviction-induced truncation from client-side early-cancel.
- Draft a short Console UX mock for evidence-request flow and preview modal.

End of note.
